findings.finding: Every consensus row cites nm_av_estimates, dated 2026-11-01. It cannot be cited until 2026-11-03 (ticker-trace lists it under sources_not_yet_citable), and the feed has not been revised for the 2026-10-29 print: the Q3 estimate is still 874.9M against the actual 895.0M, and the Q4 revenue estimate of 1,045M sits above the 1,000-1,030M guide. AV does not state the EPS basis. Any expectation-gap or 'street' comparison built on these rows uses a stale expectation that cannot be cited yet.
findings.where: gather/numbers.json consensus nm_cons_rev_fy2026, nm_cons_rev_fy2027, nm_cons_eps_fy2026, nm_cons_eps_fy2027, nm_cons_rev_q4_2026, nm_cons_eps_q4_2026; source nm_av_estimates
findings.fix: Keep consensus out of drivers, events and key_risk. Next to the result, state that consensus was pulled 2026-11-01, is not yet citable, predates revisions after the print and has an unstated EPS basis. Or rerun with as_of on or after 2026-11-03 with refreshed estimates.

findings.finding: The note's arithmetic is wrong: FY2026 consensus 3,391.3M does not equal 9M actual plus the pre-print Q4 estimate (2,363.3 + 1,045.3 = 3,408.6). It does match H1 actual + pre-print Q3 estimate + Q4 estimate (663.4 + 804.9 + 874.9 + 1,045.3 = 3,388.5). This supports the 'not revised' conclusion even more strongly; only the explanation is wrong.
findings.fix: Reword: FY2026 consensus = H1 actual + pre-print Q3 estimate + pre-print Q4 estimate.

findings.finding: The macro facts give revenue by region with unit 'USD thousands' (e.g. 1882595), while every other lane uses whole USD for the same lines (dc_seg_us_9m 1882595000). The values are correct (checked against the 10-Q and 10-K: US FY2025 1,785,554k; RoW 416,952k = 2,202,506k - US), but the mixed scale risks a 1000x error if a consumer ignores the unit.
findings.where: gather/macro.json facts mc_f_rev_us_9m26, mc_f_rev_row_9m26, mc_f_rev_us_q326, mc_f_rev_row_q326, mc_f_rev_us_fy25, mc_f_rev_row_fy25, mc_f_rev_us_fy24, mc_f_rev_row_fy24

findings.finding: dc_search_referral_drop records -1,000,000 'referrals_per_week' with basis 'reported'. The call says search traffic dropped by MORE THAN 1 million referrals per week on average during October: a management statement and a lower bound, not a reported fact.
